summary: The study describes the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of Ge–Sb films using GeCl2-dioxane and Sb(SiEt3)3 precursors at 100 /C14C, followed by tellurization annealing with tBu2Te to form Ge–Sb–Te (GST) films. The ALD process yielded a Ge-to-Sb ratio of approximately 2.2, and the tellurization temperature influenced the phase transition and composition of the resulting GST films. At 230 /C14C, the films were fully tellurized to form a uniform GST composition of Ge3Sb2Te6, with the elimination of carbon impurities.
evidence: We studied the atomic layer deposition (ALD) and the tellurization of Ge –Sb ﬁlms to prepare conformal crystalline Ge –Sb–Te (GST) ﬁlms and to achieve void-free gap ﬁlling for emerging phase-change memory applications. ALD Ge –Sb ﬁlm was prepared by alternating exposures to GeCl 2-dioxane and Sb(SiEt3)3 precursors at 100 /C14C. The growth rate was 0.021 nm per cycle, and the composition ratio of Ge to Sb was approximately 2.2. We annealed the ALD Ge –Sb ﬁlms with a pulsed feeding of di( tert-butyl)tellurium. The ALD Ge –Sb ﬁlms turned into GST ﬁlms by the tellurization annealing. When the tellurization temperature was raised to 190 /C14C or higher temperatures, the Raman peaks corresponding to Ge –Sb bond and amorphous Ge –Ge bond disappeared. The Raman peaks corresponding to Ge –Te and Sb –Te bonds were evolved at 200 /C14C or higher temperatures, resulting in the phase transition temperature of 123 /C14C. At 230 /C14C or higher temperatures, the entire ﬁlm was fully tellurized to form a GST ﬁlm having a relatively uniform composition of Ge 3Sb2Te6, and the carbon impurities in the as-deposited ALD Ge –Sb ﬁlm were eliminated.
